claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding are prone to detrimental Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
A thin CrSi2 layer placed between the Cr coating and Zr-alloy substrate will suppress high-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Suppressing Cr–Zr interdiffusion with the CrSi2 layer will prevent premature coating failure.
The CrSi2-modified coating will retain protective-oxide formation under approximately 300°C subcritical-water conditions.
The CrSi2-modified coating will retain protective-oxide formation in accident-relevant steam up to approximately 1200°C.
The CrSi2 interlayer reduces the mobility of Cr and Zr atoms across the coating/substrate interface.
The CrSi2 interlayer maintains a stable and distinct layered structure during exposure.
CrSi2 is thermodynamically stable under the proposed service and accident conditions.
CrSi2 has a low interdiffusion coefficient with both Cr and Zr.
Minimizing Cr–Zr mixing prevents formation of deleterious intermetallic phases.
Cr–Zr intermetallic phases are responsible for premature degradation of the unmodified coating.
The outer Cr coating can form a protective oxide despite the presence of the CrSi2 interlayer.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated control, the CrSi2-modified system will have a significantly thinner Cr–Zr interdiffusion zone.
Relative to the control, the CrSi2-modified system will exhibit improved coating integrity.
The proposed benefit depends on selecting a CrSi2-layer thickness and integrity that do not compromise coating adhesion.
The long-term stability of the CrSi2 interlayer under repeated thermal cycling is undetermined.
